summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent spawns a PTY driven by a remote WebSocket server (full-host RCE)
details: On startup the agent connects to a configured WebSocket server and dispatches `terminal_create`/`terminal_input` messages into a `node-pty` session on the installer's host: `message-router.js` routes `terminal_input` to `handleTerminalInput`, which writes the network-supplied bytes directly into the PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)` where `msg` comes from `ctx.ws.on('message')`. The receive→PTY.write path is unconditional once the socket is authenticated, and the same channel supports remote-triggered file writes and an `upgrade_agent` self-update. The effect is that whoever controls the server side of the WebSocket can run arbitrary shell commands on the machine running the agent, with the invoking user's privileges. Additionally, `index.js` `ensureYeaftSkills()` unconditionally clones or `git pull --ff-only`s `https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git` at HEAD (no commit pin) on every startup, copies the tree into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/` and `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, chmods files under `hooks/` to 0755, and sets `enabledPlugins` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so any future commit to that repo's default branch is auto-registered as an executable Claude plugin on the next start.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
